question: In the book Fraternity: Constitutional Norm and Human Need, what is the central theme explored by the author?

options.text: The economic inequality caused by globalization
The legal history of the Indian Constitution
The idea of fraternity as a binding force in democracy
The role of federalism in India's political system

solution:
The correct answer is __**The idea of fraternity as a binding force in democracy**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Fraternity** is a central theme in the book "Fraternity: Constitutional Norm and Human Need" authored by **Prof. Ashwini Kumar.** The book explores how the concept of fraternity serves as a moral and constitutional principle that binds citizens together in a democracy. 
• The idea of fraternity emphasizes **solidarity, mutual respect, and collective responsibility** among citizens, ensuring that democracy is not just a system of governance but a culture of cooperation and shared values. 
• Fraternity is one of the core principles enshrined in the **Preamble of the Indian Constitution**, alongside liberty, equality, and justice. The book delves into how this principle is integral to achieving social harmony and true democracy. 
• The book addresses the challenges posed by **economic inequality, social divisions, and political polarization**, arguing that fraternity can act as a unifying force to bridge these gaps. 
• Prof. Ashwini Kumar emphasizes that fraternity is not just a legal concept but also a moral necessity for fostering inclusion, dignity, and human dignity in a democratic society. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Fraternity in the Indian Constitution:** 
• **Fraternity** is explicitly mentioned in the **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution, emphasizing the promotion of **dignity of the individual** and **unity and integrity of the nation.** 
• The concept aligns with the **vision of the founding fathers** like Mahatma Gandhi, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and Jawaharlal Nehru, who envisioned a society free from caste, class, and communal divisions. 
• **Relation to Democracy:** 
• Fraternity is essential for the functioning of a **vibrant democracy**, as it fosters mutual respect and understanding among citizens, ensuring that democracy thrives on cooperation rather than conflict. 
• It addresses issues such as **social exclusion, discrimination, and inequality**, which can undermine the democratic fabric of a nation. 
• **Challenges to Fraternity:** 
• Economic disparities, social divisions, and political polarization pose significant challenges to achieving fraternity in society. 
• The book highlights the role of **policies and governance** in promoting fraternity by addressing these challenges through inclusivity and equitable distribution of resources. 
• **Examples from History:** 
• The principle of fraternity played a key role in the **Indian freedom struggle**, uniting people across diverse backgrounds for a common cause. 
• Historical movements like the **civil rights movement** in the USA also emphasize the importance of fraternity in achieving social justice. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Prof. Ashwini Kumar:** The author of the book is a noted academician and political thinker who has extensively written on democracy and constitutional values. 
• **Preamble of Indian Constitution:** The Preamble declares fraternity as one of its guiding principles to ensure **national unity and integrity**. 
• **Human Need:** Fraternity is not just a constitutional norm but a **basic human need** that fosters belongingness and dignity. 
• **Global Perspectives:** The concept of fraternity is relevant globally, as seen in the principles of **Universal Declaration of Human Rights** and other international charters promoting equality and solidarity. </ul
